title: Cloud zone GPU availability map + fallback windows — Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the operating map for zonal GPU availability and the program of fallback windows across cloud providers for North America (NA), Europe (EU), and APAC for Q3 2026. It is intentionally ops-focused: clear triggers, TTLs, and responsibilities so SRE, infra procurement, and capacity planning can act without ambiguity during hotspots or provider disruptions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers public cloud zones we operate in (primary: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, europe-central-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1).
- All numbers are capacity-reserve-equivalents (logical GPU units normalized to our m40-equivalent baseline for planning).
- Time horizon: July 1 — Sep 30, 2026.
- Scenarios: Conservative / Baseline / Surge. Baseline is the planning default.
- Fallback windows = short-lived cross-region or lower-tier model routing policies to relieve pressure.

Executive summary:
- Baseline capacity meets forecasted demand in NA/EU with 8–12% warm buffer. APAC shows tighter runway (3–6% buffer) under baseline; recommend two tactical actions: a small APAC spot buffer pool (150 GPU-equivalents) and a staged fallback window to EU for latency-tolerant batches during peak APAC evenings.
- Define pre-authorized fallback windows (30–72 hour durations) with automated routing rules and communication playbooks so traffic shifts are safe and reversible.

Capacity map (normalized GPU-equivalents):
- Baseline capacity (end of July 2026):
  - NA: 6,400 GPUs (expected utilization: 62% baseline load)
  - EU: 3,200 GPUs (expected utilization: 58%)
  - APAC: 1,800 GPUs (expected utilization: 71%)
- Conservative demand (80th percentile demand spike):
  - NA demand spike: 5,600 -> headroom 800 (12.5%)
  - EU demand spike: 2,900 -> headroom 300 (10.3%)
  - APAC demand spike: 1,740 -> headroom 60 (3.3%)
- Surge demand (95th percentile sustained for 48h):
  - NA demand: 6,800 (shortfall -400) -> fallback required
  - EU demand: 3,450 (shortfall -250) -> use EU warm pool burst
  - APAC demand: 2,200 (shortfall -400) -> cross-region routing to EU / NA fallback window

Fallback windows design (policy):
- Window types:
  1) Local burst (zone-level warm pool) — immediate; TTL 24h; requires autoscaler ramp policy.
  2) Cross-region Tolerant (route low-priority or latency-tolerant batches to nearest alternate region) — TTL 30–72h; requires customer routing rules and notice for dedicated tenants.
  3) Degradation mode (serve quantized / smaller model variants for non-critical routes) — TTL flexible; automated by Optimize recommendations.

Triggers (automated + manual):
- Auto-open local burst when: zone-utilization > 78% p95 sustained for 2h OR p95 latency degradation > 1.4x baseline for 1h.
- Auto-escalate to cross-region tolerant routing when: cluster-wide warm-pool + spot buffer < 8% AND latency or error budget breaches persist for 4h.
- Manual escalation (on-call SRE) when external provider status indicates degraded GPUs in a region or availability zone drain initiated by the cloud provider.

Fallback TTLs and rollback policy:
- Local burst TTL: 24h. If still needed at TTL expiry, a 1-hour re-evaluation window runs; if metrics remain above thresholds, extend by 24h with exec notification.
- Cross-region TTL: 30–72h depending on predicted provider recovery. Rolling rollback must be gradual (max 30% traffic shift per 30 minutes) to monitor error profile.

Operational checklist for opening a fallback window:
1) SRE runbook: confirm metric triggers and record event in incident tracker (JIRA/INC-xxx).
2) Notify product/CS leads for any potentially affected customers (pre-approved message templates exist).
3) Enable model-mix routing: shift non-SLA routes first.
4) Ramp cross-region routing at 15/30/30 percent increments per 30m while monitoring error delta and p95 latency.
5) Telemetry: enable high-fidelity traces and token-level cost/latency sampling for the duration.
6) Post-mortem: 72h after the window closes, include cost delta and customer impact metrics.

Week-by-week rollout timeline (July — September 2026):
- Week 1 (July 1–7): Deploy fallback policy automations to staging; run tabletop and dry-run across NA->EU and APAC->EU routing.
- Week 2 (July 8–14): Create APAC spot buffer (150 GPU-equivalents) and test warm-pool scaling.
- Week 3 (July 15–21): Enable telemetry gating for cross-region routing and add routing flags in prod config.
- Week 4 (July 22–31): Kick off customer-notification runbook rehearsals with CS.
- August: Monitor weekday peak windows for APAC evenings; run two scheduled simulated fallback windows (one NA, one APAC) during low-risk hours to validate rollback.
- September: Evaluate Q3 learnings and finalize Q4 pre-commit capacity adjustments.

Risk register (top items & mitigations):
- Provider sudden drain in a major NA zone -> Mitigation: pre-provisioned cross-zone warm-pool + SLA-backed vendor escalations; prioritize high-SLA routes.
- Cost delta from cross-region reroutes -> Mitigation: limit reroute TTL and route least-costly batch classes first; pre-calc cost impact in playbook.
- Increased tail latency for routed traffic -> Mitigation: progressive ramp + automatic rollback threshold at p95 > 2x baseline.

Telemetry + KPIs to track during windows:
- Zone utilization (5m, 1h), codified threshold alerts at 78% and 86%.
- P95 latency per route and per model variant.
- Error rate (5xx) delta by origin and by routed destination.
- Cross-region network egress cost delta and token-level cost.
- Customer impact score (CSAT proxy) and number of affected API keys.

Responsibilities matrix (short):
- SRE: execute runbook, metric verification, incident tracker owner.
- Capacity planning: maintain warm-pool sizes and spot buffer, update forecast weekly.
- Solutions/CS: customer notifications and SLA routing exceptions.
- Product/Optimize team: enable degraded model stacks and quantization fallbacks where appropriate.

Open questions / decisions to finalize by July 10:
- Approve APAC spot buffer reservation costs (finance sign-off required).
- Confirm customer notification SLA windows for Dedicated tenants during cross-region reroutes.
- Decide whether to allow cross-region routing for embeddings-heavy workloads (higher cost) or limit to generation + chat.

Appendix — quick capacity table (end-July baseline vs surge):
Region | Baseline (GPUs) | Expected Util (%) | Surge Peak (GPUs) | Shortfall
NA     | 6400             | 62%               | 6800             | -400
EU     | 3200             | 58%               | 3450             | -250
APAC   | 1800             | 71%               | 2200             | -400

Notes: the above shortfalls are inputs to the fallback-window planning calculator (linked in artifacts).

Action items (next 7 days):
- [Owner: Capacity planning] draft finance ask for APAC 150-GPU spot buffer (due Jul 8).
- [Owner: SRE] enable auto-open trigger for local burst in prod and test in staging (due Jul 6).
- [Owner: CS] prepare customer notification templates for Dedicated customers; include opt-out instructions (due Jul 9).

Comments / informal notes:
- Prior convos with cloud vendor indicate potential region maintenance windows in mid-August — we should schedule the August simulated fallback during vendor low-risk window to validate our rollback.
- This doc intentionally short on low-level implementation detail (see linked PRs and runbooks). The objective here is a single page operating map to be referenced in incidents.

Last edited notes:
- 2026-07-02: Added progressive ramp percentages and APAC spot buffer recommendation (Arjun).
- 2026-06-18: Initial draft and capacity normalization (Maya).
